No price was set on quality: Atlas-M costs $44 less per 1,000 conversations than Atlas-L and trails it only on overall quality; Brisk-S is cheapest but slips on safety checks.

Each step up the price frontier buys overall quality at a rising price per point, and no check separates Atlas-M from Atlas-L. The pick flips with the price the owner puts on a point of overall quality, and with any floor set on the safety checks.

!
Confidence: High, if the caveats below aren't material.
  • Nothing declares what is good enough. It moves the pick, not the figures: with no bar, floor or price per point declared, the option follows whatever price the owner sets, so the report prices the trade and leaves the call to the concierge owner.
  • A judge is not described. Only if the unstated judge of the pass/fail checks reads Brisk-S or Open-70B more harshly than the Atlas models; the price frontier itself rests on overall quality, whose judge is calibrated on 200 human ratings at 86% agreement.
  • No arm is the control. Only if a paired reading on the same cases would separate Atlas-L from Atlas-M on a check; every gap here combines each model's own interval as independent, which reads wider than a paired one, so pairing could only sharpen a gap, not reverse the frontier's order.
  • The pick is the best of several candidates. Only if a fresh run reads Atlas-L's lead over Atlas-M lower than its +2.96 pooled points (unpaired interval +1.981 to +3.939); a smaller lead raises the price of each point bought on to Atlas-L and favours Atlas-M.
  • Cost routing unknown. Only if another provider serving any of these models would reorder their costs; the run names no provider for any model, so each cost is this run's routing, not the model's own.
The tradeAtlas-L leads Atlas-M by +2.96 points of overall quality, pooled over traffic, and costs $44 more per 1,000 conversations. Atlas-M leads Brisk-S by +5.13 points, costs $25 more, and leads it on the safety checks too.
Where the answer flipsBrisk-S is the best buy if a point of overall quality is worth less than somewhere from $4.15 to $6.11 per 1,000 conversations; Atlas-L if it is worth more than somewhere from $11.09 to $22.05; Atlas-M in between. A price inside either band is not settled by this run.
Our leanOurs, not a declared rule: Atlas-M, for any price per point in the middle band. No pass/fail check tells it apart from Atlas-L, while Brisk-S's saving comes with drops on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes.
Why not the othersOpen-70B is off the price frontier on point estimates only: its pooled lead over Brisk-S is +0.79 points, interval -0.1893 to +1.769, so a point bought on to it could cost as little as $3.11, inside Brisk-S's band. What clearly counts against it: it confirms before account changes 17 points less often than Atlas-M, and trails Atlas-M on overall quality in every task but persona small talk.
WatchNo line was declared, so there is no weakest margin to watch. Speculation bait carries 0% of traffic: its decline rates say what each model does when baited, not what live traffic meets. Every cost is this run's provider routing, which is unnamed.
What would settle itThe concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or a floor on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes; either turns the trade into a call.

Next steps

  • The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or floors on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes. Turns the trade into a call: which band the price falls in names the model.
  • Measure a routed option as its own arm: Open-70B on persona small talk, Atlas-M on everything else, on the same cases. Whether routing the small talk keeps Atlas-M's safety checks at a lower cost; nobody ran this mix, so no figure states its cost or quality yet.
  • State which judge scored the pass/fail checks and calibrate it against human ratings. Turns the judge caveat on the safety checks into evidence, so Brisk-S's and Open-70B's drops can be read as absolute rates.
  • Re-score Atlas-L and Atlas-M paired on the same cases. Whether any check separates them; read independently, the tool-call check would need 1,555 cases per model to separate its gap four times in five.
  • Name the provider serving each model in the cost records. Whether the cost order is the models' or this run's routing.

Method

Cases
Each model ran 1,190 cases over the same tasks; none was lost or failed. Repeats are not stated.
Overall quality
An ordinal score from a judge calibrated on 200 human ratings, at 86% agreement, read in every task.
Pass/fail checks
Each check is read only in its own task. The input says neither who judged them nor what makes a pass beyond each check's name.
Pooled overall quality
Task means weighted by traffic share: billing 42%, persona small talk 24%, troubleshooting 19%, research 15%; speculation bait carries 0%, so it enters no pooled figure.
Intervals
At the level each block prints, uncorrected. With no control and no paired contrast, a gap between two models combines each one's own interval as if they ran different cases, which reads wider than a paired interval would. The frontier is read on point estimates; where an interval leaves a step open, the page says so.
Cost basis
Cost per 1,000 conversations as served in this run, with no provider named for any model. No monthly volume was declared, so no monthly figure is stated.
Latency
Median and p95 per task; no budget declared, and whether the models shared a machine is not stated.
Not declared
No control, no gate, floor, margin or price per point; the call is the concierge owner's.
Source
Synthetic example data from docs/eval-report-kit/references/r1-model-selection.json, run 2026-10-21.

Review findings left open

  • Must fix · The page: The confidence reads High while the cost-routing caveat stays open, and its clause misstates what would make it matter. The clause says 'Only if another provider serving any of these models would reorder their costs'. But the call is a set of price-per-point bands built from cost gaps: price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point is $14.76, which is $44 over +2.96 points. A provider charging differently for any model moves the bands without reordering anything. Rewrite the clause to say: the $4.15–$6.11 and $11.09–$22.05 bands hold for this run's unnamed routing; a different provider price for any model shifts where the pick flips, even with the cost order unchanged; the High applies to the quality figures and to the bands as priced in this run. Otherwise drop the form to low.
  • Should fix · The page: 'Why not the others' says a point bought on to Open-70B 'could cost as little as $3.11, inside Brisk-S's band'. That $3.11 is price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired, and it falls below the $4.15–$6.11 band, not inside it. A reader will look for $3.11 within $4.15–$6.11 and not find it. Write: 'as little as $3.11, below the $4.15–$6.11 band, where Brisk-S would otherwise be the best buy'. That matches what the explore row already says.
